title: Unbounded right derivation commutes with exact postcomposition
statement: Let C, D, E be abelian categories with chosen unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume C admits K-injective resolutions in the monomorphic-resolution sense used by the source library. Let F:C→D and G:D→E be additive functors, and suppose G preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Write RF and R(F⋙G) for the unbounded right derived functors computed by K-injective resolutions [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], and D(G) for the functor induced by termwise exact application of G. There is a canonical natural isomorphism R(F⋙G) ≅ RF⋙D(G). No exactness or preservation of K-injectives is required of F, and no K-injective resolution hypothesis is imposed on D or E.

source.place: Proved declaration CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso, CompositionExactRight section; exact-functor descent is Stacks Tag 015F (literature/stacks-project/derived.tex, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor).

proof.text: Since G is exact, termwise G preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so it induces D(G). Compose the unit of RF with D(G), using the termwise composition identification, to obtain the unit from the homotopy functor of F⋙G to RF⋙D(G). On a K-injective complex in C, the unit of RF is invertible, hence so is its image under D(G). The K-injective derivability structure therefore makes this composite a right derived functor. This is the existing proved isRightDerivedFunctor_rightDerivedFunctor_comp_mapDerivedCategory instance in the source module.

Uniqueness of right derived functors gives the canonical unit-compatible natural isomorphism from R(F⋙G) to RF⋙D(G). This is precisely the proved source definition rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso; its body is rightDerivedUnique applied to the two units. This works for unbounded complexes, arbitrary additive F, and also zero categories or zero functors.
